captureEviction.rule: data/history/** holds every captured ladder; THIS MODULE carries a window on it. selectCaptures() keeps the newest 12 ladders per market plus one per horizon mark (6h, 12h, 24h, 48h, 96h, 240h), and the market cap (80) then drops whole contracts. Ladders outside that window are EVICTED FROM THIS MODULE, never from data/history.
captureEviction.effect: a desk-season round whose batch this module no longer carries cannot be walked again, so the season re-reports FEWER rounds than it already measured; the desk loses the older cut-offs it could once price. The ladders are still in data/history/** — nothing was deleted.
captureEviction.reproduce: node scripts/generate-desk-module.mjs --max-captures 40 --out src/desk-data.js   # then node scripts/run-desk-season.mjs
captureEviction.batchRule: the same rule src/desk-season.js uses: capture instants are grouped while the gap to the batch's last instant is <= 20 minutes, and a round is stamped at the LAST instant of its batch
captureEviction.nothingDeletedFrom: data/history/** (the store is append-only; only this generated module is a window on it)

rule.rounds: Every round is a REAL capture instant taken from the store (a moment this repository actually queried GET /markets/{ticker}/orderbook). No round time is invented and no ladder is re-anchored.
rule.carry: Cash, open positions and resting orders carry from round to round. Between two rounds the book is walked through the real events in that window: later captured ladders, later captured candlesticks (real traded quotes) and the exchange’s own settlements.
rule.resting: A resting order placed in round N is alive in round N+1: a later real quote that trades through its price crosses it, bounded by the size that later ladder showed or the volume that period really traded.
rule.marks: Every entrant is marked at every round boundary from a captured quote, a captured ladder mid or the exchange settlement value — never from an invented price. A position with no captured mark is carried at cost and the MARK record says so.
rule.settlements: A finalized contract pays $1.00/$0.00 by its own `result`/`settlement_value_dollars` at its own `settlement_ts`. A NO position is paid notional minus that value. No settlement fee is charged (official schedule).
rule.caps: The liquidity cap is cumulative across the season per contract, so a season can never fill more real contracts than the contract’s own volume base supports.
rule.mandate: Maximum return only: no stop-loss, no position cap, no volatility target. The season publishes what that costs (drawdown from the round-by-round equity curve).
